KMX fiscal year ends late February, so VA FY-2022 (revenue $31,900M) is roughly calendar 2021 and FY-2023 roughly calendar 2022; KMX was aligned one label ahead (FY-2022 vs FY-2023) to match CVNA FY2021 vs FY2022. From Q1 2026 reported revenue includes traditional gross revenue treatment for vehicles from a large retail marketplace partner, which lowers the margin denominator-side; year-over-year comparisons normalize from Q3 2026 (CFO, doc 110739).

company.note: CVNA had no prior margin peak to reverse: FY2021 0.50% was its first positive year, FY2025 11.01% is its all-time high, and 13.5% is a new high. Revenue rose 6.2% into the FY2022 trough while retail units fell 3% (Q4 2022 call summary, doc 225076); revenue then fell to $10,771M in FY2023.

peers.excluded: PAG (commercial truck and UK mix), parts retailers (AZO, ORLY, AAP), OPENLANE, Valvoline, non-US dealers and Auto1; six closest US used and franchised auto retailers kept.
peers.note: Median of six = average of GPI and LAD in both years. Peers held record margins through 2022; their compression came in 2023 to 2025 (GPI 6.93% to 4.34%, LAD 7.30% to 4.96%) while CVNA expanded. FY2025 CVNA was +636 bps above the peer median (GPI/LAD average 4.65%).

deciding_facts: Over FY2021 to FY2022 CVNA adjusted EBITDA margin fell 815 bps (0.50% to -7.65%) on revenue up 6.2%, while the six-peer auto retail median slipped only 38 bps (7.50% to 7.11%): ratio 0.05, relative gap widened from -700 to -1,477 bps.

Management's own account is capacity built for growth that did not come ('we built capacity in most of our business functions for significantly more volume than we fulfilled'), and the 2023 to 2025 recovery to 11.0% (+636 bps over peers) happened while peer margins compressed, so both the trough and the path to 13.5% are self-help, not cycle. The 2026 gross revenue treatment cuts reported margin (Q2 2026 10.4% vs 12.4%) without changing EBITDA dollars, so the street's FY2026 10.22% understates the like-for-like run rate.
